html:
The Kumeyaay, known to the Spanish as Diegueño, are a Yuman-speaking people of the borderlands of southern California and northern Baja California, from the San Diego coast inland to the deserts. The name also covers the closely related 'Iipai and Tiipai.

They moved with the seasons between coast, mountains and desert, gathering acorns, agave and seeds, fishing and hunting, and shaping the land with fire. In 1769 Junípero Serra founded Mission San Diego de Alcalá in their land, the first of the California missions. In 1775 hundreds of Kumeyaay attacked and burned it, one of the first revolts against Spanish rule in California. In 1848 the new US and Mexican border cut their land in two; today there are about a dozen Kumeyaay bands in the US and several communities in Mexico. Their neighbours were the Luiseño, the Cupeño and the Quechan.
